official.application_route: Apply directly to the Johns Hopkins Neuroscience PhD via applygrad.jhu.edu by early December; no separate Janelia application, but name one to four Janelia group leaders in the Statement of Interest.
official.study_mode: Full-time; one year in residence at Johns Hopkins in Baltimore followed by research years at a Janelia laboratory
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or residency restriction is published for admission; Johns Hopkins notes that only U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals and U.S. permanent residents are eligible for U.S. NIH funding, so funding for international students is more limited.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible to apply; TOEFL or IELTS is required unless waived for applicants who studied at a university in the U.S. or earned a degree where English was the primary language of instruction. Johns Hopkins states funding for international students is more limited and that international applicants who secure outside support often exhibit the characteristics of successful applicants.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Neuroscience PhD at Johns Hopkins with thesis research at HHMI Janelia Research Campus; published research areas include behavioral and systems neuroscience, cellular and molecular neuroscience, evolution and genetics, instrumentation and computational tool development, neuronal cell biology, optical physics and imaging, structural biology and biochemistry, and theory and computational neuroscience.
official.research_requirement: The Statement of Interest and Career Objectives must state interest in doing thesis research at Janelia Research Campus, list one to four Janelia Group Leaders, and briefly describe interest and goals in those labs. Laboratory research experience is desirable. The thesis defense takes place at the partner institution (Johns Hopkins).
official.duration: Multi-year PhD; one year in residence at Johns Hopkins followed by the remaining research years at Janelia, with the degree granted by Johns Hopkins
official.description: The Janelia Joint Graduate Program is a fully-funded, collaborative PhD program for independent, committed graduate scholars, run in partnership with the Solomon H. Snyder Department of Neuroscience at The Johns Hopkins University. Graduate scholars spend their first year at the partner university and then reside at Janelia for the remaining years of the program to conduct their thesis research; degrees are granted by Johns Hopkins and each scholar has a research mentor at Janelia and a programmatic mentor at Johns Hopkins.
official.english_requirement: TOEFL or IELTS required for international graduate scholars; scores must be received before the application deadline and reported to JHU Institution Code 5316. The TOEFL requirement is waived for applicants who completed, or are enrolled in, a degree program at a university within the U.S. or U.K., or who received a degree from an institution where English was the primary language of instruction; students who studied in Puerto Rico do not have to submit a score. No minimum score is published on the pages consulted.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the Johns Hopkins Neuroscience PhD with a designated route to do your thesis at HHMI's Janelia campus, so you submit one application to Hopkins, not to Janelia, and the whole package (tuition, stipend, insurance, programmatic travel) is guaranteed for every admitted student. Your only real lever is the one-page Statement of Interest and Career Objectives, which must name one to four Janelia group leaders whose science genuinely interests you. Interviews happen on the Hopkins recruitment visit in winter, decisions land by 15 April, and only about 14 to 16 students enter the programme each year. International applicants can and do get in, but Hopkins is explicit that NIH-funded slots are limited to US citizens, nationals and permanent residents, so plan how you will fund yourself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent B.S. or B.A. graduates with real laboratory research experience who want a fully funded neuroscience PhD and already know which Janelia labs match their interests.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist one to four Janelia group leaders, read their recent papers, and write your Statement of Interest around those labs; vague interest will not survive a holistic review.
Confirm each undergraduate institution can send transcripts and request them early; international applicants should use the approved WES service.
Ask your three recommenders now: references are entered by the applicant and submitted by Hopkins, and letters must be in by the December 3 deadline, not merely the application.
Book TOEFL or IELTS early enough that official scores reach JHU (Institution Code 5316) before the deadline, and check whether your prior U.S./U.K. study waives it.
Attend the Hopkins Neuroscience virtual open house (22 October 2026) and consider the student-run Neuroscience Application Assistance Program for statement feedback.
common_rejection_risks: Naming Janelia group leaders without explaining fit: the statement must connect your research experience and goals to those specific labs
A CV over the 2-page limit or a Statement of Interest and Career Objectives over the 1-page limit
Weak or mismatched letters from people who cannot speak to aptitude for independent research
Late-arriving recommendation letters or test scores, which make the whole application incomplete at the deadline
Thin research preparation; Hopkins favours applicants who used undergraduate summer and postbac opportunities well
Applying without grasping that the first year is coursework and rotations in Baltimore, not lab work at Janelia
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: No published stipend figure exists to net against costs, so budget yourself: the application fee (waivers are available via income, military service, or Maryland-institution alumni criteria), relocation to Baltimore before the first stipend, personal living costs beyond the stipend, visa fees, and any non-programmatic travel. Admitted students can apply for a $1,500 need-based relocation grant.
document_audit: Transcripts must be uploaded from every college attended, not just the degree-granting one; all materials must be in English and international applicants are directed to WES
The Statement of Interest and Career Objectives has a hard 1-page limit and must carry the Janelia group-leader names; do not bury them in an appendix
The Personal Statement is a separate 1-page document about a formative experience, distinct from the research statement, and applicants routinely conflate the two
CV is capped at 2 pages and must quantify full-time and part-time research months
TOEFL/IELTS official scores must arrive by the deadline; unofficial or late scores invalidate otherwise complete applications
alerts: The neuroscience deadline (3 December 2026) is earlier than other Johns Hopkins School of Medicine graduate programs, so do not plan around the SOM calendar

Interview invitations go out around mid-January and happen virtually and at Janelia during the Hopkins recruitment visit; decisions are final by 15 April, which is before the general April 15 national PhD decision date, so keep other options in play
All admitted students undergo criminal background checks as School of Medicine policy
Graduate student visas are sponsored by Johns Hopkins, not Janelia; contact the JHU international office early
Funding for international students is more limited because NIH training support is restricted to U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals and permanent residents
If you are already admitted to the Hopkins Neuroscience PhD without naming Janelia, you can still join later via a summer rotation agreed by the student, advisors and program directors
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create the application in the JHU graduate portal (applygrad.jhu.edu), upload transcripts, CV, both statements and any additional material, enter three recommenders who submit their letters directly, send official TOEFL/IELTS scores to institution code 5316, and submit before 3 December 2026; interviews follow in mid-January and decisions by 15 April.
